
# Project background

## Tumor evolution
:::{.columns}

::: {.column width="45%"}

Tumor grows and evolves under evolutionary pressure
  
  - Trophic
  - Metabolic
  - Immunological
  - Therapeutic
:::

:::{.column width="53%"}

**Intratumor heterogeneity** (ITH): diversity in genetics, phenotype, or even epigenetic profiles among cells in the *same* tumor. That diversity can help some cells survive selection pressures.

**Consequences of ITH**

- Therapeutic failure
- Drug resistance
:::

:::

![Intratumor heterogeneity of tumor cells from @walshaccurate ](/assets/images/adt/ith.png){width="60%"}

## Implication of ITH - Treatment

:::{.columns}

::: {.column width="45%"}
- ITH implies that tumor cells could (Darwinian):
  - Possess a genetic reservoir (accumulating different variations).
  - Adapt to different evolutionary pressures.

- **Treatment** is a selective evolutionary pressure (therapeutic pressure).
- Natural selection favors treatment-resistant tumor cells.
:::

::: {.column width="53%"}

![Selective pressure and drug resistance, image from @greaves2012clonal](/assets/images/adt/drug%20resistance.png){width="80%"}
:::
:::

## Prostate Cancer

:::{.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
**Prostate Cancer in Hong Kong**
In 2023

- Prevalence rate (crude): 88.2 per 100K 
- Mortality rate (crude): 15 per 100K

**Treatment**

- Radiotherapy
- Surgery
- Chemotherapy
- Hormone therapy
  - Prostate cancers are usually androgen-dependent. Hormone therapy works by reducing/blocking androgens, which can slow down or stop the growth of the cancer.
  
:::

::: {.column width="42%"}
![Prostate cancer](/assets/images/adt/prostate%20cancer.png){width=80%}
:::

:::

## Hormone therapy for prostate cancer

- Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) is used for advanced prostate cancer
- Continuous ADT
  - Disadvantages
    - Side effects (e.g., hot flashes, loss of libido)
    - Drug resistance (e.g., castration-resistant prostate cancer)
-  Intermittent ADT (IADT)
   - Advantages @perera2020intermittent
     - Delayed drug resistance
     - Reduced side effects (Improved quality of life) 

## Data sources

@bruchovsky2006final implemented a clinical trial of IADT

:::{.columns}
::: {.column width="57%"}


- **Total participants**: 103 eligible patients with prostate cancer
- Monitoring biomarkers:
  - Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels (indicates the activity of prostate cancer cells)
  - Testosterone (Effectiveness of ADT)
- Treatment protocol:
  - ADT is given for a fixed time (36 weeks) until PSA levels drop to 4 $\mu$g/mL
  - ADT is stopped until PSA levels rise to 10 $\mu$g/mL
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
![IADT protocol, image from @bruchovsky2006final](/assets/images/adt/iadt.png)
:::

:::

## Evolutionary therapeutics

:::{.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

**Adaptive therapy**

Giving "breathing room" to drug-sensitive tumors. During the low-dosage periods, drug-sensitive cells can outcompete resistant ones.

- Adjust time (Intermittent therapy)
- Dosage 

**Applications**

- Breast cancer [@enriquez2016exploiting] 
- Prostate cancer [@zhang2017integrating]

:::

:::{.column width="48%"}

![Adaptive therapy, figure from @mcgehee2024mathematical](/assets/images/adt/adaptive.png)

:::

:::

## Monitoring tumor progress

- Adaptive therapy relies on close monitoring of tumor progression
- Current practice:
  - Monitoring on tumor biomarkers
  - Monitoring on dosage levels of the drug in the blood

|  Tumor type | Monitor parameter | Study |
|  ---------- | ----------------- | ----- |
| Ovarian cancer | Serum biomarker + Tumor size  | @mukherjee2024study |
| Prostate cancer | Blood biomarker  | @zhang2017integrating |
| Melanoma | Tumor size | @smalley2019leveraging |
| Breast cancer | Tumor size | @enriquez2016exploiting |

- Implication: Some tumors are not good targets for adaptive therapy due to the management cost

## Adaptive strategy

Designing strategy to turn on- and off- the therapy also varies


| Study | Type | Rule |
| ------- | ----- | --------- |
| @mukherjee2024study | Continuous | Proportion to biomarkers |
| @zhang2017integrating | Intermittent | Proportion to tumor size |
| @smalley2019leveraging | Intermittent | Tumor size + mathematical simulation |
| @enriquez2016exploiting | Continuous | Proportion to tumor size |

## Benefits of adaptive therapy

:::{.columns}

:::{.column width="48%"}

- Delayed drug resistance
  - Delayed tumor progression
- Better clinical outcome 
- Improve quality of life @hussain2013intermittent
  - Side effects of the treatment may be reduced during off-cycles

:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
![Better outcome in metastatic colorectal cancer @avallone2025intermittent](/assets/images/adt/intermittent%20threrapy.png)
:::

:::

## Challenges in adaptive therapy

- Identifying heterogeneity in the tumor and monitoring the response to the treatment
- Ultimately kill all cancer cells is extremely challenging 
  - **Analogy**: Antibiotics, antiviral drug resistance
- Adaptive therapy tries to
  - Make the tumor manageable
  - **Not** necessarily fully cure cancer
